literal_source_claim: 波雷尔博弈的决定性 (determinacy of Borel games)
canonical_claim: For every Borel payoff set A in Baire space, the Gale-Stewart game in which two players alternately choose natural numbers and Player I wins exactly when the resulting sequence lies in A is determined: one of the two players has a winning strategy.
domain_and_universes: Play = Nat -> Nat, History = List Nat, Strategy = History -> Nat, all in Type 0; compatibility consults Player I at even history lengths and Player II at odd lengths.
quantifiers: every payoff set A contained in Baire space
a proof that A is Borel under the source-selected Baire topology
the disjunction that Player I or Player II has a winning strategy
hypotheses: players alternate natural-number moves for omega many rounds
perfect information and the source-selected winning convention
conclusion: The game is determined: one player has a strategy winning against every opponent strategy.
statement_choices_requiring_source_audit: the source's exact game and strategy definitions
whether Borel means generated from open sets in omega^omega and which topology presentation is used
the payoff convention for Player I and its complement for Player II
the foundation in which the theorem is stated and the choice or transfinite-recursion principles used
whether the paper states a broader move space or an equivalent coding
excluded_degenerate_cases: Open, closed, clopen, finite-horizon, finite-move, countable-payoff, and assumed-determined games are not substitutes for arbitrary Borel payoff sets. The axiom of determinacy and projective determinacy are separate claims.
source_status: primary_1975_paper_identified; exact statement, definitions, proof pages, assumptions, errata, immutable copy, and independent review open
